name: RenderLite
description: Performance toolkit for Geometry Dash: draw divide, process priority, power plan, focus mode, GPU preference, fast loading and anti-crash.

priority-level.name: Process priority
priority-level.description:
How much CPU time Windows gives the game.

Strongest: High.
Options: Normal (default), Above normal (medium), High (strongest).

throttling-mode.name: Power throttling
throttling-mode.description:
Stops Windows from slowing the game down to save power. Most useful on laptops.

Strongest: CPU and timer throttling off.
Options: Windows default (no change), CPU throttling off (medium), CPU and timer throttling off (strongest).

timer-resolution.name: Timer resolution
timer-resolution.description:
How precisely Windows times frames, which can make frame pacing more even.

Strongest: 1 ms.
Options: Windows default (about 15 ms), 2 ms (medium), 1 ms (strongest).

power-plan.name: Power plan
power-plan.description:
Switches the Windows power plan while the game is running. Your old plan is restored when the game closes.

Strongest: Ultimate performance (falls back to High performance if your PC does not have it).
Options: No change (default), Balanced, High performance, Ultimate performance (strongest).

background-priority.name: Background apps
background-priority.description:
Lowers the priority of your other running programs while the game is running, so the game gets most of the CPU. They are restored when the game closes. Programs started after the game opens are handled when you return to the main menu.

Strongest: Strongest.
Options: Off (default), Medium (below normal), Strongest (idle priority).

focus-mode.name: Focus mode
focus-mode.description: Turns off Windows notification pop-ups while the game is running and restores them when it closes. Windows itself does not let mods switch its Focus assist on, so this only hides the pop-ups.

gpu-preference.name: GPU preference
gpu-preference.description:
Tells Windows which graphics card the game should use. Mostly useful on laptops with two graphics cards. Restart Geometry Dash after changing this setting.

Strongest: High performance GPU.
Options: No change (default), High performance GPU (strongest), Windows default (removes the override).

draw-divide-key.name: Draw divide hotkey
draw-divide-key.description:
Press this key while playing to switch Draw divide on or off. A small message shows the new state. It only works while the game window is in front. Pick None to turn the hotkey off.

Options: None, F1 to F12, Insert, Home, End, Page Up, Page Down, Pause, Scroll Lock. Default: F8.

draw-divide.name: Draw divide
draw-divide.description:
Draws the picture at a lower frame rate than the game logic. The game still runs its physics and reads your clicks at the full FPS, but the graphics card only draws the screen at the Render FPS below. This lowers GPU load and keeps the low input delay of a high FPS.

It only does something when the game runs at a higher FPS than the Render FPS. Unlock the FPS in the game's graphics settings, or use the Game logic FPS setting below.

render-fps.name: Render FPS
render-fps.description:
How many pictures per second are drawn while Draw divide is on.

0 = match your monitor's refresh rate (recommended).
Strongest: a low number such as 30. It saves the most GPU power, but the picture looks choppier.

logic-fps.name: Game logic FPS
logic-fps.description:
How fast the game logic runs (physics and input). Maximum 480.

0 = do not change (use the game's own FPS setting).
Strongest: 200. It gives the lowest input delay. Use it together with Draw divide so the picture stays light.

fast-loading.name: Fast loading
fast-loading.description: Speeds up the Geometry Dash loading screen by letting it run at the highest possible frame rate. It works best when V-Sync is off in the game's graphics settings. It cannot speed up Geode's own loading. Restart Geometry Dash after changing this setting.

anti-crash.name: Anti-crash (experimental)
anti-crash.description: Tries to catch errors during gameplay and skip the broken frame instead of closing the game. It cannot stop every crash, and the game may behave oddly after an error. Turn it on if the game keeps crashing.
